intro: A bridge you can shop on. You are at Irgandı Bridge in Bursa province, built in 1442. It carries a market along its length, one of four bridges of this type still standing anywhere in the world, and craftspeople still work here today.
history: In 1442 the Bursa merchant Hoca Muslihiddin built this bridge, and on it a market of thirty-two shops. Then came hard times. Badly damaged by the earthquake of 1855 and by a fire, it was demolished in 1949 and replaced by a flat concrete crossing. But the story did not end there: its original form was rebuilt in 2004, and the shops were handed back to craftspeople.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the market superstructure and the row of shops, then look at the stone arch and down to the Gökdere bed.
facts: Did you know? Bridges with a market still standing on them can be counted on one hand: Irgandı and the Ponte Vecchio in Florence share the same short list. And this one was nearly lost. It was demolished in 1949 and replaced by a flat concrete crossing, before its original market form was rebuilt in 2004.
outro: This brings our journey across Irgandı Bridge to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
